title: Estimating the risk of irreversible post-SSRI sexual dysfunction (PSSD) due to serotonergic antidepressants
authors: Ben-Sheetrit J, Hermon Y, Birkenfeld S, Gutman Y, Csoka AB, Toren P
population: Men aged 21 to 49 in the Tel Aviv district database of Clalit Health Services, non-smokers with BMI below 25 and without medical or psychiatric conditions or medicines associated with erectile dysfunction; 866 treated with serotonergic antidepressants
funder: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.
authorConflicts: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.
result: Erectile dysfunction, defined by PDE-5 inhibitor prescriptions, was more frequent after serotonergic antidepressants (adjusted OR 3.2, 95% CI 2.3 to 4.4). Four of 866 treated men (0.46%, 1 in 216) met criteria for persistent post-treatment erectile dysfunction, defined as persisting at least one month after stopping without active depression or anxiety; they had used escitalopram, paroxetine, imipramine or nortriptyline for 4 to 8 months and still received PDE-5 inhibitors 3.6 to 14.8 months later. The authors note that counting only erectile dysfunction treated with PDE-5 inhibitors in healthy men may underestimate the risk.
